Great place to celebrate meat!

We came here for a birthday and the restaurant was excellent! Here is why!

FOOD:

Cochon is a great place to celebrate pork and proper Louisiana food. We started out with the sausage with beans and sun dried tomatoes, where the flavours of tart tomato clashed beautifully with the softness of the beef and the pure flavour of the sausage. We also continued with alligator bites with spicy mayo and those were tender and well balanced. For our min, we shared the Cochon, which is pulled pork formed into a patty on a plate of bacon cabbage. The dish was well done overall, but what truly stood out was the quality of the meat and the almost smokey taste of the pulled pork. The cucumber salad helped cut through the heaviness of the pork, creating a great balance. For dessert, we tried the pineapple upside down and a pretzel ice cream. I will be dreaming about this ice cream for a while!

SERVICE:

Kayla and Nick were exceptional and helped us have an awesome experience. They were extremely knowledgeable about the food, welcoming, and kept our table organized throughout the evening.

ATMO:

We were impressed with the space. However, the interior felt slightly outdated. Part of it is being an architectural design family. It is a nice restaurant, but there is definitely more opportunity here for the interior!

I went to Mother's Restaurant for a little CUP of red beans and rice and somehow left with enough food for TWO DAYS! 😂

I wasn't planning on a big meal, but then I spotted the Southern cabbage, followed by the sausage. Before I knew it, the lovely lady behind the counter said, "You might as well get the meal!" And boy, was she right! 😂

For approximately $18.75, I received a VERY generous portion of food! The grits and cabbage were so good that I literally stopped eating to record a video! That's how impressed I was.

But what really deserves recognition is the attention to detail and thoughtful service. My meal was packaged securely, with the food and all those delicious juices contained so nothing leaked into the bag. They included utensils, hot sauce, salt, pepper, and everything I needed without me having to ask.

That may sound like a small thing, but in a time when basic condiments and utensils are often overlooked, I genuinely appreciate a restaurant that thinks about the entire customer experience, not just the food.

From the friendly service and generous portions to the careful packaging and delicious Southern cooking, Mother's made a wonderful impression on me.

Sometimes it's the little things that make a BIG difference! ❤️

I'll definitely be back the next time I'm in New Orleans!

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Mother’s Restaurant is exactly what I hoped a classic New Orleans institution would be! If you’re looking for fancy, this isn’t it. If you’re looking for authentic, historic, flavorful comfort food served with heart… you’ve found it. #BestCheeseGrits in ALL OF NOLA. creamy tasty I will go back for just those! I normally don’t eat cheese grits!

Walking in feels like stepping into a piece of New Orleans history. The walls are filled with decades of memories, military pride, and stories. I especially appreciated their deep respect for veterans and the military—it adds another layer of character to an already iconic restaurant.

The food? Delicious!

Breakfast was a winner with fluffy scrambled eggs, creamy grits, and one of the thickest, juiciest sausages I’ve had in a long time. They also offer complimentary ham cracklins (think pork bacon bites), and they were a fun little New Orleans treat while waiting for our food.

We came back for lunch because everyone insisted we couldn’t leave without trying the famous Ferdi Special, and now I understand why! That “debris” roast beef is unbelievably tender and piled high. Every bite was packed with flavor.

The jambalaya was loaded with meat throughout, not just a few pieces here and there. The red beans and rice were hearty, and after adding a little Louisiana hot sauce like the locals do, they really came alive.

My absolute favorite? Those seasoned green beans! They were cooked perfectly with tomatoes, onions, and plenty of meat throughout. They may have stolen the show for me!

A huge shout-out to our server, Janette, who was every bit as memorable as the food. She was warm, funny, full of personality, and made us feel like regulars instead of first-time visitors.

One of my favorite parts was simply watching everyone around us. You could tell this is where locals and visitors alike come to enjoy a satisfying meal. There was something special about seeing people happily “scarfing down” their food because it really was that good.

The prices are very reasonable for the generous portions, and the experience is worth every penny.

Mother’s isn’t trying to be trendy. It’s preserving tradition, serving incredible comfort food, and doing it with genuine New Orleans hospitality.

Five stars from me. I’ll definitely be back the next time I’m in New Orleans! ❤️🍽️

If you're visiting New Orleans, **Brennan's is an absolute must!** From the moment we walked in, the spectacular food, elegant ambiance, and top-tier hospitality made our first visit to the city truly unforgettable.

The entire staff was incredibly warm and welcoming, making us feel like honored guests from start to finish. You can genuinely feel the pride and passion they put into every detail of the dining experience.

One thing you *have* to order is the **Bananas Foster**! Brennan's is home to the original recipe, and the tableside preparation is an experience all on its own. The staff not only prepares it flawlessly but also shares the fascinating history behind the iconic dessert, making it both delicious and memorable.

One detail that really stood out to me was the level of service. One of my biggest pet peeves at restaurants is when dishes are brought out one at a time, leaving some guests waiting while others eat. That was definitely not the case here! More than four team members came to our table together to serve every plate and drink at the same time. It was seamless, thoughtful, and made us feel like royalty.

Every aspect of our experience exceeded expectations. Brennan's isn't just a meal—it's an experience filled with exceptional hospitality, incredible food, and genuine care for every guest. Thank you for making our first trip to New Orleans so special. We can't wait to come back!

An Unforgettable Anniversary Brunch at Brennan’s!

Brennan’s was an absolutely wonderful experience from beginning to end! The atmosphere felt like a lovely, open, airy garden; elegant, inviting, and the perfect setting for a special occasion.

Our group tried a variety of dishes, and everyone loved their meal! We started with the framboise French toast as an appetizer, followed by Eggs Hussarde, duck confit waffle, crab and corn omelet, and New Orleans shrimp and grits. Every dish was delicious and full of flavor. The Bloody Bull was zesty and delicious, and the single-origin Papua New Guinea coffee was incredibly smooth and flavorful.

And the desserts? Absolutely fabulous! We all loved the bread pudding—even my husband, who normally hates bread pudding! The lemon tart was beautiful, creative, and the perfect balance of sweet and tart. The pineapple tarte tatin was equally delightful and a wonderful way to finish our meal.

The service was just as impressive as the food. Our server was attentive to our needs, and we never once felt rushed. We were there to enjoy our time together, and the staff made us feel completely welcome. To make the experience even more special, Brennan’s recognized our 24th wedding anniversary with a beautiful green ribbon across our table and a champagne toast. Such a thoughtful touch that made the occasion feel truly memorable!

We’ll be back!

I also tried the Porch drink — light, citrusy, and super refreshing on a warm day. Perfect cool-down while waiting for the order.
No fried oysters available that day (they’re often a mid-week thing usually Wed/Thurs), which was a little disappointing since they’re a highlight here, but it just means I’ll be back soon.
Parkway has that great neighborhood tavern vibe and delivers reliably tasty po’boys. The shrimp one stole the show for me. If you’re in the French Quarter, the streetcar ride makes it a fun, low-key adventure.

Commander’s Palace is absolutely worth the visit and remains a true New Orleans classic.

The atmosphere is beautiful, historic, and exactly what you hope for when dining in New Orleans. The pre-dinner bread alone is worth mentioning — honestly, it was good enough to justify the visit by itself.

The standout dish for me was the Shrimp & Tasso Henican. The combination of wild Louisiana white shrimp, housemade tasso ham, pickled okra, sweet red onions, five pepper jelly, and Crystal hot sauce beurre blanc was outstanding. It may be one of the best shrimp dishes I have ever had.

The Café Pierre Painted Texas Quail was also very good — rich, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. For dessert, the Pecan Pie à la Mode was excellent. Warm pecan pie with vanilla bean ice cream, chocolate, candied pecans, and fleur de sel caramel sauce was a perfect finish. I may never want to eat pecan pie cold again.

The only disappointment was the Commander’s Creole Gumbo. I really wanted to love it, but it fell flat for me and tasted more like brown gravy than the deep, flavorful gumbo I was expecting.

Service was good, though not quite great, especially for a restaurant of this reputation. Still, the food, atmosphere, and overall experience made it a memorable dinner. I would happily go back.

★★★★★ A Must-Visit in New Orleans

If I were returning to New Orleans, I would make a reservation at Pêche again without hesitation. In fact, it’s one of those rare restaurants that is good enough to justify a trip back all by itself.

Everything about the meal was interesting, creative, and absolutely delicious. One standout was the chickpea-floured okra, which was incredible, especially with the accompanying sauce. My son loved the local oysters, which were fresh, flavorful, and among the best we’ve had.

From start to finish, the entire meal was outstanding. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, and there wasn’t a weak spot on the menu.

The service was equally impressive. Rather than relying on a single server, the staff worked seamlessly as a team. Everyone was attentive, friendly, and proactive, creating a dining experience that felt polished without being formal or stuffy.

This ended up being my son’s favorite new restaurant of the trip, and it’s easy to see why. Pêche delivers exceptional food, excellent service, and a memorable dining experience. It’s a true New Orleans gem and, in my opinion, a must-visit restaurant. ⚜️🦪🍤🍷

Would I return? Absolutely. I’d fly back to New Orleans just to eat here again.

I came here wanting seafood but didn't really know what kind. That turned out fine because the menu made the decision for me. I started with the seafood platter, then got the wood-fired fish, shrimp toast, and a slice of bread pudding. Somewhere in there I realized I had ordered enough for a small table.

The seafood platter was a fun way to start because there was a little bit of everything going on. The shrimp toast was probably the sleeper favorite for me. It was crisp, savory, and disappeared much faster than expected. The wood-fired fish had that smoky edge that makes grilled seafood so good, while still tasting fresh underneath. Bread pudding was probably an unnecessary final move, but it was warm and soft and had just enough sweetness to finish things without sending me into a sugar coma.

The restaurant has a good amount of energy without feeling like a tourist trap. You can tell people are there because they genuinely want seafood, not just because they happened to walk by. I'd definitely put this back on the list next time I'm in town.

I love this place. It’s consistent, friendly, and delicious. Make sure it's on your list for your next New Orleans trip!

I stayed at this property over Mother’s Day weekend for an staycation, and overall my stay was pleasant. The room itself was great, and the one issue I had with the water pressure was handled immediately and professionally.

My concern is with the way I was treated during breakfast at Pete’s on the morning of May 9th.

I was seated by a Black woman with an accent who was very welcoming. However, after being seated, I sat for over 10 minutes without being acknowledged or assisted while guests who were seated after me were greeted and helped almost immediately. Eventually, the manager, Justin, came over to greet me and take my order. He explained that they were very busy and that he was stepping in to help. While I did observe him assisting around the restaurant by removing dishes and handing out refills, I did not witness the restaurant being sooooo busy to where management HAD to step in and take orders as majority of the people there were already eating.

Once my food finally arrived, I needed ketchup and once again sat for several minutes without assistance until the bartender, Sandee, stepped in to help me. She was the only person who consistently checked on me, offered to refill my water and coffee, and made an effort to ensure I had what I needed.

As I explained to Sandee while visibly upset and crying, people work very hard to be able to enjoy certain environments and experiences, and it is deeply hurtful to feel overlooked or as though they do not belong. Watching other guests receive immediate attention while I repeatedly sat unassisted made me feel singled out and, honestly, discriminated against in that moment. That experience left me embarrassed and emotional, and it put a very negative cloud over what otherwise would have been a great stay. I do want to acknowledge Sandee for her kindness and attentiveness, because she was the one person who made me feel seen and cared for during that experience..

Dining at Antoine’s truly feels like stepping back into the golden era of New Orleans. Established in 1840, this legendary restaurant is not only historic, but filled with soul, elegance, and timeless Creole charm. The restaurant features around 14 uniquely themed dining rooms, each carrying its own atmosphere and stories, decorated with fascinating photographs of famous artists, political figures, and important personalities who once dined there.

The service was exceptionally elegant and professional — classic fine dining hospitality that is becoming harder to find today. Every detail felt refined yet warm, making the entire experience memorable from start to finish.

The food was absolutely delicious. I highly recommend trying the escargot and the onion soup, both rich in flavor and beautifully prepared. Their liquor selection and cocktails were also excellent, perfectly complementing the sophisticated atmosphere of the restaurant.

Antoine’s is more than just a place to eat — it is a living piece of New Orleans history, where tradition, culture, and fine dining come together in the most unforgettable way. A true must-visit when in New Orleans.

If you spend time in New Orleans, Antoine’s must be on your list to visit.

We started with fresh oysters: delicate, sweet taste with a fresh finish, Brussels sprouts: pleasantly sweet and nutty with a crunchy topping,  and the tuna crudo, which was delicate and tasty. They have a varied selection of wines and cocktail options. I had the Sauvignon Gris, which was refreshing and crisp.The staff was top-notch!
There was some street parking, but you could also park at the nearby hotels.

text.text: The food is delicious! First time I’ve ever dared to try stuffed oysters and the shrimp stuffed oysters were incredible - we ordered three rounds. The bread loaf was a little underwhelming in comparison, but the trout dip and crackers tasted delicious and crawfish appetizer as well. A majority of our table ordered the shrimp and grits since it’s a staple down here and it was well received. The red beans and rice were yummy but the fried chicken and honey on top really sealed the deal on that dish! Beautifully light space inside, with decent service (our meal did take quite some time and we came at the tail end of the lunch so I wouldn’t come here in a hurry).

If you're looking for a classic New Orleans dining experience, the Court of Two Sisters is worth adding to your list.

The buffet is a great way to sample many of Louisiana's signature dishes in one meal. Rather than committing to a single entrée, you can explore the flavors that have made New Orleans one of America's great food cities.

Start with the turtle soup. It's a true Louisiana classic with a rich, savory flavor that reflects the city's deep culinary traditions. Whether it's your first bowl or your fiftieth, it's one of those dishes every visitor should try.

Be sure to save room for dessert. The warm bread pudding, topped with whiskey sauce, is everything you want it to be. Soft, comforting, and rich without being overly sweet. It's the perfect ending to a classic Creole meal.

The beautiful courtyard adds to the experience, making it feel like you've stepped into another era of New Orleans. Between the historic setting, the wide variety on the buffet, and iconic dishes like turtle soup and bread pudding, the Court of Two Sisters offers a meal that's as much about tradition as it is about great food.

If you want to experience classic Louisiana cuisine in one sitting, this is a great place to start.

The pasta, the filets, and the duck were excellent but the star of the night was the pork chop which was phenomenal!! We topped off the meal with bread pudding which was delicious!

Our server, Jeremiah, was amazing!!

This was the perfect place for a meal after a concert at Preservation Hall.

We really enjoyed our stay at Windsor Court in New Orleans. From the moment we arrived, we loved the elegant and welcoming atmosphere of the hotel. The location was perfect for us, making it easy to walk around and enjoy everything the city has to offer.

Our room was lovely, comfortable, spacious, and beautifully decorated. We also really enjoyed the swimming pool, which was a wonderful place to relax and take a break from exploring the city.

One of the things that stood out to us was the concierge. They were incredibly helpful and friendly, and always made us feel well taken care of.

We also loved the live music at the hotel. There’s something very special about sitting back with a drink, listening to great music, and enjoying that unmistakable New Orleans atmosphere.

It was a lovely experience, and we would definitely come back!

After four visits to New Orleans, I can honestly say it has become my favorite city to visit—and Windsor Court has become my favorite place to stay there. I have stayed at Windsor Court on three of those four trips, including both a suite and the Club Level, and I already know I’ll be returning on future visits.
The hotel itself is beautiful, elegant, and perfectly located for enjoying New Orleans. But what keeps bringing me back is the feeling of being genuinely cared for as a guest.
The Windsor Court Spa has been an especially meaningful part of my last two visits. Brennan Rosonet, the Spa Director, has been exceptional. She has been incredibly helpful not only with recommendations within the spa, but also with suggestions for enjoying the city. She took the time to understand what I was looking for and made recommendations that helped make my visits to New Orleans even more enjoyable.
As a transgender woman, being completely authentic and comfortable in a new environment can sometimes be difficult. At the spa, I experienced exactly the opposite. I was treated with warmth, professionalism, and respect, and I was consistently gendered appropriately. Brennan even took the extra step of making sure my reservations reflected my preferred name. Those details may seem small, but they meant a great deal to me. I felt seen, respected, and genuinely welcome.
There are two things I hope Windsor Court will continue working on.
While my experiences at the spa have been wonderful, I was unfortunately misgendered at times elsewhere in the hotel. I understand that mistakes happen, but consistency throughout the property would make an important difference for transgender guests. The spa has demonstrated how welcoming that experience can be, and I would love to see that same level of awareness throughout the hotel.
I also really appreciate the evening turndown service. It is a lovely touch and one of the things that makes staying at Windsor Court feel special. During my visits, however, the timing seemed somewhat inconsistent, which occasionally made it difficult to plan my evening around giving staff access to my room. A more predictable window would make an already thoughtful service even better.
Those concerns are small compared with the overall experience I’ve had at Windsor Court. I love this hotel. I love the way it feels, I love the location, I love the spa, and I appreciate the genuine hospitality I’ve experienced here.
Most importantly, I plan to come back.
New Orleans has become my favorite city to visit, and Windsor Court has become an important part of that experience for me. I share this feedback because I value the hotel and want to see an already wonderful experience become even better.
I’m already looking forward to my next visit.
